_note: The declared effect of every supported invocation: what it writes, what it sends, and the test case that proves it. One row per command, per subcommand and per effect-changing flag (vocabulary.effect_changing_flags). A row is not publishable without its effect test — scripts/check-effects.mjs refuses one, and refuses a flag from that list that a help usage line carries and no row declares. Read this with docs/effects.md.

annotations.readOnlyHint: The invocation changes nothing: no file under the target, the working directory or the user's machine, and no request off the machine. The command-lifecycle journal counts — a journal append is a write like any other, so every readOnlyHint: true row is an invocation the CLI exempts from lifecycle capture (the converse does not hold: some journal-exempt invocations, such as demo and the --no-write forms, still write other declared files).
annotations.destructiveHint: The invocation can overwrite, clear or discard state that existed before it ran (a waiver over a blocking gate, a cleared run session, an overwritten verdict or assembly report). Only meaningful when readOnlyHint is false.
annotations.openWorldHint: The invocation can contact an endpoint off this machine. True exactly when the row declares at least one send.
annotations.idempotentHint: Repeating the invocation with the same arguments adds no effect beyond the first run.

tiers.none: No effect: nothing written anywhere, nothing sent.
tiers.B: Writes: files are created or updated under the target, the working directory or the user's machine. Nothing leaves the machine.
tiers.A: Sends: the invocation can contact an endpoint off this machine (it may write locally too).
tiers.C: Destructive: the invocation overwrites, clears or discards state that was already there (it may send too).
tiers._ranking: A row carries the HIGHEST tier it can reach, ranked none < B < A < C.

locations.{target}: The target the invocation names: the directory given to --target, or the Page Kit target repository the Build Packet points at.
locations.{cwd}: The working directory the invocation runs in.
locations.{packet}: The Build Packet the invocation names (--packet), wherever it lives — it need not be the copy inside the target repository.
locations.{spec}: The CampaignSpec file the Build Packet names (spec.local_path), which need not live inside the target repository.
locations.{home}: The user's machine: the home directory and the config root under it (XDG_CONFIG_HOME when set).
locations.{lifecycle-journal}: The command-lifecycle journal wherever it was selected for the invocation — the active run session's journal, --lifecycle-journal, or CAMPAIGNS_OS_LIFECYCLE_LOG.
locations.{proxy-base}: The endpoint --proxy-base names, or the canonical NEXT endpoint when it does not.
locations.{base-url}: The campaign under test, as --base-url names it or as the packet derives it.
locations.{map-id}: The saved Map the CampaignSpec identifies.
locations.{playwright-download-host}: Where Playwright fetches browser builds from: PLAYWRIGHT_DOWNLOAD_HOST when set, else the Playwright CDN (cdn.playwright.dev). The third-party browser download used by `qa install-browser` and `tooling setup`.

conditions.no_session: No run session at the target or the working directory.
conditions.ambient_session: An active ambient run session opened by `run start` at the target.
conditions.stale_session: A run session at the target idle past the 12 h TTL, and one at the working directory too.
conditions.lifecycle_log: CAMPAIGNS_OS_LIFECYCLE_LOG names a journal outside the runtime directory.
conditions.persisted_consent: Run Telemetry consent PERSISTED on the machine for the loopback receiver's scope — the record `telemetry on --proxy-base <loopback>` writes — with no CAMPAIGNS_OS_TELEMETRY override, a synthetic campaign key in the environment, no run session, and the receiver named by --proxy-base wherever the command takes one. The condition exists because consent must not be read from the row under test: under the other four the fixture switches consent on only for rows that DECLARE a consent-gated send, so a send nobody declared ran with consent off and left no trace. Here every row runs consented, and any request the receiver sees that no declared send covers fails the row.

test_scope.full: The invocation executes past its preflight in the offline fixture, so every declared write and send with a non-empty observed_in is observed by the test.
test_scope.preflight: The invocation cannot execute past its preflight offline (a browser, a live gateway, a real credential, a real store). The test proves the preflight refusal writes nothing beyond what the row declares, and — where a loopback receiver can stand in for the destination — that the declared destination IS the one contacted.

vocabulary.observed_in: The conditions in which the effect test must SEE this write or send. An empty list declares an effect the offline fixture cannot reach; it then requires a not_observed_reason, and check-effects refuses the row without one. The test always refuses an effect that is NOT declared, in every condition.
vocabulary.preflight: What the preflight itself may do, on a `test_scope: "preflight"` row, declared apart from the effects the row declares for the invocation that gets past it: `may_write` is the complete list of paths the refusal may write (no `**` — an allowance that licenses a subtree licenses the home directory the refusal must not touch) and `may_contact` the exact request paths the loopback receiver may see. The test enforces both independently of `writes`/`sends`, so a write declared for the success path cannot license the preflight to write there.

sends.when: Run Telemetry consent is on for the endpoint, --no-remit and --no-write were not given, and the packet's campaign key resolves

rows.notes: next self-decides the stage. The local capture always happens; the .remit.json envelope beside each snapshot records what the delivery did. It SENDS the progress observation: the snapshot captured under .campaign-runtime/progress/ is POSTed to {proxy-base}/api/progress when Run Telemetry consent resolves ON for that endpoint and the packet's campaign key resolves. Consent persisted for the endpoint (`telemetry on --proxy-base <url>`) is what reaches it; a CAMPAIGNS_OS_TELEMETRY=on override alone does not, because an env grant carries no scope and the remit refuses an unscoped grant for a non-canonical endpoint (scope_bypassed). That is why the four session conditions — which run with consent off for a row declaring no consent-gated send — saw no request, and why this row once declared none.

rows.notes: PREFLIGHT-PROVED: the one-time browser install cannot complete with no network — it downloads the Chromium build from the Playwright CDN. This is the only row in this file whose send is not a Campaigns OS endpoint, and the only one that writes the user's machine outside the config root. The case proves the failed install writes exactly one path there — the registry's link entry — and nothing else anywhere, and that the download attempt leaves the machine zero times. The registry is PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH when set, else the platform browser cache under the home directory (~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright on macOS, ~/.cache/ms-playwright on Linux, %LOCALAPPDATA%\ms-playwright on Windows); the fixture pins it to {home}/ms-playwright so the proved path is the same on every platform. Not destructive: an already-installed revision is left alone, which is also why the run is idempotent. Runs the Playwright CLI bundled with THIS package, never whatever `npx playwright` resolves to.

rows.notes: PREFLIGHT-PROVED: checks the selected project copy, exact pin, installed page-kit and context preservation before attempting the package-owned browser download. The closed-loopback fixture fails that download before global skills, context or project instructions change. After a successful download, setup composes the existing installers and appends the context import once. Does not read gateway credentials, resolve or close campaign run sessions, append journals, remit telemetry, scaffold pages or create campaign evidence. Focused tests prove rerun preservation, refusal-before-write and browser-failure recovery.
Checks the selected project and previews the existing skill/context installers and instruction import without downloading a browser, touching credentials or recovering/remitting a run session.
